name: Mexico
snapshot: Mexican forces killed the boss of the Jalisco cartel in 2026, but a US indictment of a sitting governor from Sheinbaum's own party showed the pressure only growing.
culture: Mexico's culture draws on Aztec, Maya and other Indigenous civilisations and on Spanish colonial heritage. Día de Muertos, mariachi, lucha libre and a cuisine on UNESCO's heritage list are global icons. Frida Kahlo and Diego Rivera's murals defined modern Mexican art, and its filmmakers, like Guillermo del Toro and Alfonso Cuarón, lead Hollywood.
society: Mexico is the United States' largest trading partner, and its factories are deeply woven into North American supply chains. Cartels control territory, extort businesses and drive a homicide rate that has topped 30,000 a year. More than 100,000 people are officially missing. Morena's dominance and a judicial overhaul have raised concerns about checks and balances.
situation: For two decades, Mexico's governments have fought drug cartels, and the cartels have mostly won: more than 400,000 people have been killed since 2006, and large parts of the country are governed in practice by criminal groups. In 2026, under heavy pressure from a Trump administration that designated the cartels as terrorist organisations and threatened to send US troops, Mexico struck harder than ever and found the pressure only grew.

In February, Mexican forces killed Nemesio Oseguera, "El Mencho," the leader of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel, the country's second-largest criminal group, in an operation backed by US surveillance; it was the first time forces under President Claudia Sheinbaum had taken out a cartel boss of that stature (Al Jazeera). By January, Mexico had already handed 92 alleged cartel figures to US custody. Then, on 29 April, US prosecutors in New York indicted Rubén Rocha Moya, the sitting governor of Sinaloa, and nine other officials from Sheinbaum's own Morena party, including a senator and the mayor of Culiacán, accusing them of helping the sons of "El Chapo" Guzmán in exchange for political support and bribes (CSIS). Sheinbaum demanded evidence, called the key exhibit "a sheet of paper with names and figures," and refused to extradite him; Rocha took leave and was summoned by Mexico's own prosecutors instead (Revista E&N). Analysts noted the indictment landed in the middle of talks over the USMCA trade pact, on which Mexico's economy depends. Mexico also co-hosted the World Cup, which opened in Mexico City in June.
power: A federal presidential republic. The president is directly elected for a single six-year term; Congress has a Senate and a Chamber of Deputies, both now dominated by Morena. A 2024 judicial reform made judges, including the Supreme Court, elected by popular vote.
holders: President Claudia Sheinbaum (Morena), in office since October 2024, Mexico's first woman president.
